current.text: Kennard signed with Phoenix in free agency.
He comes off the bench. The projected starters are Jalen Green, Devin Booker, Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges and Oso Ighodaro.
Too many guards are ahead of him in Phoenix for him to make a real fantasy impact.
Booker, Green, Brooks, Bridges and Gillespie are expected to take most of the Suns' touches, which leaves little usage for bench players.
One expert expects him to shoot about 40 to 41% from three on around eight attempts a game off the bench. That would mean more volume at a lower percentage.
His fantasy role is a three-point streamer who sometimes adds assists.
His Yahoo status is questionable with a knee issue.
Phoenix has the best fantasy schedule in the league. It plays 4-4-4 games in the playoff weeks and has the fewest back-to-backs.

durable.text: He made 48% of his threes last season but took only about three a game in about 22 minutes.
He is one of the best three-point shooters by percentage ever. He is a pure shooter who has always taken too few threes.
He does not get to the rim and is not a mid-range shooter.

note: Kennard is ranked 262 on Yahoo and 221 on ESPN, and both sites value him at 0 USD. That puts him well outside our 144-player draft, so do not draft him. He is a bench shooter with few turnovers (0.8 a game) and good FG% on low volume (about 53% on under 6 attempts). The Yahoo FT% projection of 67% clashes with his past rate of about 90%. Watch him on waivers early. Check his knee and whether his three-point attempts rise toward the projected eight a game. If they do, Phoenix's 4-4-4 playoff schedule makes him a useful streamer for threes in weeks 19 to 21.
